title: Exponential quantum speedup for linear-system image classification on large feature matrices
claim: A quantum linear-system solver trains a regularized linear classifier on MNIST and CIFAR-10 feature matrices of size 1000000000 by 1000000000 with rank 50 and condition number 10. The matrix comes with sample-and-query access, and the solver returns a sample from the output probabilities of the solution to precision 0.05. Its cost is polylogarithmic in N. We claim an exponential advantage over classical CNN baselines of matched accuracy.

check.evidence: dequantizable: sample-and-query access; rank 50 <= log2(N)^2 = 894; output is a sample or a scalar. A classical sampler runs in poly(k=50, kappa=10, 1/eps=20) * polylog(N) (Tang 2019, arXiv:1807.04271; Chia et al. 2020, arXiv:1910.06151)

title: Quantum magnetic Laplacian inversion for directed fraud-cycle ranking

title: Exponential speedup for recommendation-style regression via quantum linear-system solving
claim: For a matrix with 1073741824 rows (30 qubits), rank 50, condition number 10, given with sample-and-query access, our quantum linear-system routine returns the probabilities of the solution's computational-basis outcomes to error 0.05 in time polylogarithmic in 1073741824, against a solver that must read the matrix: an exponential separation for recommendation-style regression. We verify the scaling on synthetic instances up to 30 qubits and expect the gap to persist at full size; negative only if runtime tracks rank.

title: Shallow entangling-circuit probability features for independence-polynomial counts at 64 nodes
claim: A 64 qubits circuit applying H on all qubits, CX along the chain, S on all qubits, then H on all qubits, starting from |0...0> and measured in the computational basis, gives output probabilities that serve as features for maximum-independent-set count labels. On 2000000 graph instances of 64 nodes, these features predict the counts with lower error than Glauber Monte Carlo independence-polynomial estimates at an equal shot budget. The gap should persist at sizes where brute-force enumeration is out of reach.

check.evidence: family claimed at 64 qubits, checked at widths 4, 6, 8; at 8: Clifford: all 16 generators X_i, Z_i conjugate to Pauli strings under the 31 gates that affect the output (31 in all, 8 qubits), so Gottesman-Knill simulates it in poly(n)

check.twin_easy: easy: middle-cut Schmidt rank 1 < 4 at width 4, so a low-bond MPS simulates it

title: Entangled-layer sampler for million-row generative modeling beyond classical reach
claim: We pitch a 64 qubits circuit family that applies H on all qubits, then a CX chain, then S on all qubits, then a second layer of H on all qubits. It starts from the all-zero input and is measured in the computational basis. We claim the output probabilities give a model of correlations in a dataset of 1000000 rows that no classical sampler can match at 64 qubits. The entangling CX chain and the interference from the final H layer should yield a quantum advantage for generative modeling, and we propose to confirm it on hardware.

title: Entangling-chain features on 3-regular graphs where WL is blind
claim: On 1000000 random 3-regular graphs with 64 nodes, where 1-WL features are constant, a 64 qubits circuit applying H on all qubits, a CX chain, S on all qubits, then H on all qubits, with probabilities read out in the computational basis, gives features that classify maximum-independent-set count labels above 90 percent while spectral features stay below 75 percent. title: Entangling phase-layer features for independence-set count labels at 64 qubits
claim: On 64 qubits, a fixed feature circuit applies H on all qubits, then CX along a chain, then S on all qubits, then H on all qubits, and reads out probabilities in the computational basis. We claim that kernel features built from these probabilities beat a tuned Gaussian-kernel ridge regressor by at least 3 points of accuracy on maximum-independent-set count labels, on a training set of 1000000 rows of graphs with 14 to 16 nodes. The advantage comes from the interference pattern that the entangling chain and the phase layer create across the register.

title: Fidelity kernel on 64 qubits for graph-feature classification at 2000000 rows
claim: A fidelity kernel on 64 qubits, prepared with H on all qubits, then RY on all qubits rotating qubit i by x_i at scale 1.0, then RX on all qubits at scale 0.5, beats a tuned RBF kernel by 3 AUC points on 2000000 rows of graph-structured features with maximum-independent-set count labels. Kernel entries are estimated from measurement probabilities of the overlap circuit, and the gain holds across 5 random splits at a fixed budget of 8000 shots per entry.

check.evidence: family claimed at 64 qubits, checked at widths 4, 6, 8; at 8: product state: every one-qubit marginal is pure on 5 random inputs (min purity 1.000000000000), so k(x,x') factorizes into 8 one-qubit kernels, O(n) classically

title: Hardware fidelity kernel on 50 qubits that beats RBF baselines at a million rows
claim: A fidelity quantum kernel on 50 qubits uses a feature map of H on all qubits, then RZ on all qubits, then RY on all qubits, with one feature per qubit setting each rotation angle. We train on 1000000 rows of 50 features. Kernel entries are read out as the expectation value of the projector onto the encoded state, estimated on hardware. We claim a quantum advantage: test accuracy above tuned RBF, gradient-boosted and neural baselines, which saturate on this task, with the gap persisting as the training set grows.

title: Fifty-qubit fidelity kernel for 2000000-row transaction anomaly ranking
claim: On 50 qubits, a fidelity kernel feature map built from H on all qubits, then RZ on all qubits with angle equal to feature x_i, then RY on all qubits with angle 0.5 x_i, will beat a tuned RBF kernel by at least 3 points of AUC on a 2000000-row transaction anomaly ranking task with 50 features per row. title: Quantum linear-system solve for detector-error correlations in surface code decoding
claim: A quantum linear-system solver applied to a detector-error correlation matrix defined by a formula of the lattice geometry, with N 1000000000000, rank 50 and condition number 10, given with sample and query access, returns the logical-fault expectation value to additive error 0.05 in time polylogarithmic in N. Exact classical solution at this scale needs about 1e15 operations. This gives an exponential speedup for calibrating decoder weights on large surface code patches, and the expectation value is the only quantity the calibration needs.

title: Quantum linear solver for Rydberg magnetometry calibration
claim: A quantum linear-system solver calibrates a Rydberg sensor array on Ramsey magnetometry traces. The response matrix has N 1000000000000 and rank 50, with sample access to its rows and norms through QRAM, condition number 10. The solver returns the expectation value of the fidelity observable that the calibration needs, to additive error 0.05, in time polylogarithmic in N. Conjugate gradient on the same system needs work linear in N, so the quantum solver is exponentially faster at this scale.

title: Polylog sampling of the solution of a trillion-dimensional linear system
claim: For a matrix of size 1000000000000 with rank 50 and condition number 10, given by sample access to its rows and entries from a formula for the coupling coefficients, a quantum linear-system solver draws from the probabilities of the solution amplitudes to precision eps 0.05 in time polylogarithmic in N. Direct classical solution costs over 1000000000000000 operations, and the draws locate the dominant response regions, which is all the application needs. We expect an exponential speedup in N, to be measured against the best published classical solver.
